name: Maaseiah
overview: Maaseiah was a male figure in the post-exilic community who played a significant role during the public reading and explanation of the Law under Ezra's leadership. He is notably recognized for standing on Ezra's right hand as the Law was read and explained to the people, indicating a position of honor and responsibility. Additionally, Maaseiah's name appears on the sealed covenant document, reflecting his commitment to the community's covenantal obligations.
namesAndTitles: The name Maaseiah means 'YHWH is a refuge,' highlighting a theological affirmation of God's protection and care. This proper name, recorded in Nehemiah 8:4, reflects the faith-centered identity of the individual without indication that the name was given directly by God.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture infers that Maaseiah was a descendant of Levi, connecting him to the priestly tribe. Beyond this, no other family relationships are explicitly recorded in the biblical text.
scriptureSignificance: Maaseiah's presence beside Ezra during the public reading of the Law underscores his role in supporting the spiritual restoration of Israel after the exile. His inclusion among those who sealed the covenant document demonstrates his active participation in reaffirming the community's dedication to God's commandments. Together, these details highlight Maaseiah as a committed leader who contributed to the reestablishment of covenant faithfulness among the returned exiles.
